certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Code of Practice. Since IS 15556 : 2005 is a laboratory testing methodology rather than a direct physical consumer product, it does not carry an individual mandatory BIS 'ISI Mark' product stamp on its own. However, compliance with its sampling, sample digestion, and chemical calibration protocols is strictly required in laboratory accreditation audits (under NABL ISO/IEC 17025:2017), state pollution control board compliance audits, and public procurement chemical audits across India.

requirements.detail: Prescribes two volumetric methods—potassium permanganate titration and potassium dichromate titration—suitable for analyzing samples with higher concentrations of iron (typically greater than 2 percent by mass).
Prescribes two spectrophotometric methods—thioglycolic acid and o-phenanthroline—designed to measure trace levels of iron in parts-per-million or parts-per-billion ranges.

Ferric iron (Fe3+) is reduced to ferrous iron (Fe2+) using stannous chloride (SnCl2) in a hot hydrochloric acid medium. The excess SnCl2 is neutralized using saturated mercuric chloride (HgCl2), which forms a silky white precipitate of mercurous chloride (Hg2Cl2).

To prevent hydrochloric acid from being oxidized by the titrant, Zimmermann-Reinhardt solution (containing manganous sulphate, phosphoric acid, and sulphuric acid) is added prior to titrating against standard 0.1 N potassium permanganate. Phosphoric acid complexes with yellow Fe3+ ions to form a colorless ferric phosphate complex, ensuring a sharp pink endpoint.

Similar reduction is performed using stannous chloride and mercuric chloride. The Fe2+ ions are subsequently titrated against standard potassium dichromate solution in an acidic medium using diphenylamine or sodium diphenylamine sulphonate indicator to yield a sharp violet-blue endpoint.

Thioglycolic acid reduces trivalent ferric iron (Fe3+) almost instantaneously to divalent ferrous iron (Fe2+), while simultaneously reacting with the Fe2+ ions in an alkaline ammonium hydroxide medium to form a highly stable, intensely colored reddish-purple coordination complex measured spectrophotometrically at 535 nm to 540 nm.

Ferrous iron (Fe2+) reacts with 1,10-phenanthroline to form an orange-red chelate complex, [Fe(o-phen)3]2+, which is measured spectrophotometrically at 510 nm. Any Fe3+ present in the sample must first be quantitatively reduced using thioglycolic acid or hydroxylamine hydrochloride to estimate total iron.

Iron content in ppm (as Fe) is calculated using the formula: Iron (as Fe) ppm = C * 25 / W, where C is the concentration of iron from the standard calibration curve in micrograms per milliliter (ug/mL), and W is the weight in grams (g) of the sample contained in the test aliquot.

Observed or calculated test or analytical values must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be identical to the specified limit in the material standard.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 15556 : 2005 is the primary national Indian Standard test specification establishing unified, high-precision laboratory test methods for the quantitative volumetric and spectrophotometric determination of iron. Formulated by the CHD 1 sectional committee and reaffirmed in 2022, the standard amalgamated two older independent standards (IS 4264 and IS 4542). It unifies four essential analytical methodologies: volumetric potassium permanganate titration (using Zimmermann-Reinhardt solution) and potassium dichromate titration for higher concentrations of iron (greater than 2%), and trace-level spectrophotometric methods utilizing thioglycolic acid (forming a reddish-purple complex) and o-phenanthroline (forming an orange-red chelate), supporting accurate chemical testing, environmental testing, and material certification across India.
